jobs.title: Registered Environmental Health Specialist
jobs.description:
**Approximate Salary**

$6,790.73 - $8,254.17/month

  

**Opening Date**

10/6/2026 1:00:00 PM

  

**Closing Date**

10/9/2026 5:00:00 PM

  

**Employment Type**

Full-Time

  

**Analyst**

Ricardo Perea

  

**Introduction**
----------------

The San Joaquin County Environmental Health Department is recruiting to fill one full-time Registered Environmental Health Specialist vacancy and to establish an eligible list which may be used to fill future vacancies.  
  
**\*Additional 4% increase effective July 2027**
  
  
Resumes **will not** be accepted in lieu of an application. A completed application must be postmarked or received online by the final filing deadline.  
  
**Pre-Employment Drug Screening and Background:** Potential new hires into this classification are required to successfully pass a pre-employment drug screen and a background investigation as a condition of employment. Final appointment cannot be made unless the eligible has passed the drug screen and successfully completed the background process. The County pays for the initial drug screen.  
  
***NOTE: All correspondences relating to this recruitment will be delivered via e-mail. The e-mail account used will be the one provided on your employment application during time of submittal. Please be sure to check your e-mail often for updates. If you do not have an e-mail account on file, Human Resources will send you correspondences via US Mail.***

**TYPICAL DUTIES**
------------------

* Conducts inspections and investigations to determine environmental health problems; determines needs for corrective action and provides appropriate assistance; conducts surveys and collects data.
* Enforces and obtains compliance with federal, state and local laws, ordinances, regulations, and standards in the area of environmental health.
* Inspects food handling and processing establishments, land use applications, public swimming pools and spas, substandard housing, well systems, small public water systems, on-site wastewater treatment and disposal systems, underground storage tank facilities, hazardous waste generator facilities, and other environmental health programs; performs emergency response services.
* Reviews and approves plans for installation of on-site wastewater treatment and disposal systems, well systems, underground storage tanks, public swimming pools, food establishments, small public water systems and other related environmental health installations.
* Investigates complaints of nuisances such as vector problems, waste disposal and other unsanitary conditions; gathers facts, collects samples and prescribes abatement and control measures.
* Inspects chemical and hazardous waste storage facilities and investigates hazardous material spills.
* Gathers, organizes and analyzes technical data and prepares appropriate reports utilizing computers and computer software programs; maintains specialized records; prepares correspondence.
* Interprets environmental health laws and regulations to contractors, public and private officials and the general public; makes presentations to various interest groups.
* Provides information for the preparation of billing statements, issues environmental health permits and collects fees.
* May assist in training of Environmental Health Specialists and Environmental Health Specialist Trainees.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**
--------------------------

**Education:** Possession of a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with course work in sciences and mathematics as prescribed in Section 106600-106735, all inclusive, of the California Health and Safety Code.  
  

**Registration:** Possession of a valid certificate as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist issued by the California Department of Health Services.

  

**License:** Possession of a valid California Driver’s License.

**KNOWLEDGE**
-------------

Basic principles of biology, chemistry, microbiology and physics; principles and practices of environmental health; federal, state and local laws, regulations and standards relative to the duties; agencies, officials and resources involved in the environmental health field; principles and methods of conducting investigations and inspections, methods for resolving problems and enforcement procedures; safety practices; language mechanics; methods of data gathering, analysis and presentation, including statistical concepts; mathematics at the college algebra or calculus level; basic public relations principles.

**ABILITY**
-----------

Conduct inspections, investigations, and reporting procedures; enforce laws and develop satisfactory resolutions of problems and violations; interpret technical written information; communicate effectively with others, both orally and in writing; present information in both written and verbal formats; operate a data entry device; establish and maintain effective working relationships with a wide variety of public and private business officials and the general public; follow written and oral instructions.

**PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS**
--------------------------------

Mobility-Operation of a data entry device; repetitive motion; sitting, standing, walking for extended periods of time; driving; occasional pushing, pulling, bending, squatting, climbing; Lifting-Frequently 5 pounds or less; occasionally 5 to 30 pounds; Visual-Distinguishing between various items, including pests and health conditions; constant good overall vision and reading/close-up work; frequent color perception and use of eye/hand coordination; occasional use of depth perception and peripheral vision; Hearing/Talking-Frequent hearing of normal speech, hearing/talking on the telephone, talking in person; Emotional/Psychological-Frequent decision making, concentration, and public contact; deal with emergency situations, exposure to trauma, grief, death; heights; working with hazardous materials; Special Requirements-Some assignments may require working weekends,

jobs.title: Environmental Chemist
jobs.description:
**Job Overview:**

The APTIM Federal Services, LLC team is seeking a Field Chemist to support an existing project team at our Hunters Point Naval Shipyard Project in San Francisco, California along with other projects in and out of the Bay area as well as California in general. This position will support a variety of Field and Office/Remote Chemistry-related tasks on all phases of project activities. Environmental Laboratory experience is desired, but not a requirement.

**Key Responsibilities/Accountabilities:**

* Planning and oversight and/or completion of on-site sample collection and packaging and shipping of samples
* Coordinating with subcontract laboratories
* Interpretation/evaluation and verification/validation of chemical data
* Assist in the development of plans, including selection of sampling and analyses methods
* Data tracking and evaluations against project criteria
* Preparation of procedures and reports related to sample/data collection and results
* Communication of data and comparison to decision-limits to project teams, including client and/or regulator entities, ensuring conformance to applicable technical standards as well as company policies and procedures
* Participation in project planning and execution should results indicate additional action is required

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Ability to work individually as well as cooperatively and be an important member of a remediation field team
* Ability to prioritize assignments and work independently with minimal guidance
* May act as a resource for colleagues with less experience
* Monitor and control costs within own work. Solve moderately complex problems; take a new perspective on existing solutions
* Manage own time to meet agreed targets
* Ability to work outside in all weather conditions and on sites where hazards are present and PPE is required
* Able to lift up to 40lbs
* Possess ability to explain difficult issues, develop and plan solutions, and work to establish consensus
* Promote teamwork; coaches and guides others.
* Possess a BS Degree in Chemistry or other Environmental/Physical Science discipline
* Looking for 1-3 years relevant experience, with experience in environmental investigation/remediation sampling and analysis a plus.

**About APTIM**

APTIM enhances the quality of the environment, wellbeing of people, resilience of communities, and opportunity for employees to make a difference, not just a living. A leading professional solutions firm, we specialize in environmental, sustainability, resilience, and infrastructure solutions. Our team of experts provide these integrated solutions for forward-thinking government agencies, commercial and industrial clients, and energy customers. Together, we create sustainable and resilient communities for all.

What you can expect from APTIM:

* Work that is worthy of your time and talent
* Respect and flexibility to live a full life at work and at home
* Dogged determination to deliver for our clients and communities
* A voice in making our company better
* Investment into your personal and professional development

As of the date of this posting, a good faith estimate of the current pay range for this position is $35.00 to $43.00 per hour. Compensation depends on several factors including: experience, education, key skills, geographic location of the position, client requirements, external market competitiveness, and internal equity among other employees within APTIM.

**Employee Benefits**

APTIM Federal Services, LLC is committed to providing an extensive range of benefits that protect and promote the health and financial well-being of our employees and their families through the APTIM Benefits Marketplace https://aptim.makeityoursource.com/.

* Medical, vision, and dental insurance: Through the marketplace, our employees can choose benefits from five metallic levels and several carriers to find the right benefits that work for them in their location.
* Company paid and optional Life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability insurance
* Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity coverage
* Paid holidays, vacation, and sick leave (eligibility based on company policy and applicable law)
* 401(k) APTIM offers three 401k plans through the Aon Pooled Employer Plan (PEP). The specific plan you are eligible for depends on the business unit you are in. The details of the largest plan are found here:
* + APTIM 401(k) Guide
  + APTIM - Helpful Documents

**Watch our video:**  
**About APTIM - In Pursuit of Better**

jobs.description:
Job Posting: AIR POLLUTION SPECIALIST

State Air Resources Board

JC-532324



AIR POLLUTION SPECIALIST
  
AIR POLLUTION SPECIALIST

$5,918.00 - $11,455.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **10/27/2026**

**Application Methods:**

Electronic (Using your CalCareer Account)

By Mail

Drop-off

Print Job

Save Job

### **Job Description and Duties**

The Emissions Certification and Compliance Division is recruiting an Air Pollution Specialist (APS) for the Heavy-Duty In-Use Compliance (HDIUC) Section. This section is responsible for the largest heavy-duty engine recall in history. For an engineer or scientist, this is the stuff of dreams: getting out of the ordinary and making a difference in people's lives by helping to reduce in-use emissions so that we can all enjoy cleaner air. The heavy-duty on-road and off-road in-use compliance programs are essential to protect public health by helping to guarantee that the stringent engine emissions standards are met in-use and are remedied through recall or possible enforcement action.

This job requires the APS to be a project manager for the in-use engine/equipment emissions testing programs, review in-use testing data submitted by manufactureres, conduct emissions compliance and defeat device analysis, review and process recalls to correct noncompliance, and support CARB enforcement actions and rulemaking efforts. The APS will be working with various California Air Resources Board (CARB) groups, manufacturers, and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to support testing, facilitate discussions, and investigate emissions noncompliance issues.

For the CARB-run in-use compliance programs, the APS will create test plans, direct procurement of vehicles/off-road equipment (evaluating proper operation and maintenance), collaborate with various CARB sections to have vehicles instrumented, and coordinate testing. The successful candidate will perform engineering analysis of emissions test data and complex technical information, generate clear and concise technical reports, and organize/present the results.

For the manufacturer-run in-use testing programs, the APS will review and process in-use compliance test reports and coordinate with manufacturers on the completion and compliance of the testing. The APS may also travel to testing sites and manufacturer's emissions test facilities to perform laboratory audits and verify compliance. Travel is expected to be up to 10% of the time and may include overnight or multi-day trips. Depending on the activity, travel may involve flying or driving a car or truck. In some cases, work outside of normal hours may also be required. Safety footwear and safety glasses are required.

Throughout these processes, the APS will communicate and coordinate with the engine manufacturer to support testing and when necessary, develop corrective actions, review and process voluntary/influenced recalls, and track their implementation. The APS will support CARB enforcement staff with litigation or settlement actions for in-use compliance investigations when necessary. The APS will aso support CARB ruelmaking efforts related to in-use compliance requirements.

In addition, the APS may be called upon to serve as a lead staff person for work groups and technical meetings, and to engage in outreach events with industry, government organizations, and the public.

The candidate must have excellent verbal and written communication skills to engage with a variety of stakeholders, as well as create and review technical documents.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

This position may be eligible for hybrid in-office work and in-state telework. The amount of telework is at the agency's discretion and is based on the California Air Resources Boards' (CARB) current telework policy. While the CARB may support telework, some in-person attendance is also required.

The positions at the CARB may be eligible for telework with in-person attendance based on the operational needs of the position under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria outlined in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of hybrid telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location at their own expense, as indicated on their duty statement.

Effective July 1, 2025, the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025). PLP 2025 directs that each employee shall receive a 3 percent reduction in pay in exchange for 5 hours PLP 2025 leave credits, monthly. The salary range(s) included in the job advertisement do not reflect the 3 percent reduction in pay.

* Standard office environment (artificial lighting, controlled temperature, etc.)
* Daily use of a personal computer, office equipment, and/or telephone.
* High Physical Demand: safety footwear is required for hazardous work conditions when working in the lab or field which may include: transportation and set-up of gas cylinders for laboratory audits, and set-up for emissions testing (vehicle emission testing, emission control component inspections, vehicle maintenance activity, etc.).

jobs.title: (Senior) Environmental Scientist / (Senior) Industrial Hygienist
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

**Are you looking to join an organization that is growing and dynamic? What about a high-energy, collaborative environment that rewards hard work?**

J.S. Held is a global consulting firm that combines technical, scientific, financial, and strategic expertise to advise clients seeking to realize value and mitigate risk. Our professionals serve as trusted advisors to organizations facing high stakes matters demanding urgent attention, staunch integrity, proven experience, clear-cut analysis, and an understanding of both tangible and intangible assets.

The firm provides a comprehensive suite of services, products, and data that enable clients to navigate complex, contentious, and often catastrophic situations.

 **Job Description**

J.S. Held is seeking an experienced and highly motivated **(Senior) Environmental Scientist / (Senior) Industrial Hygienist** to join our Industrial Hygiene & Built Environment practice in Los Angeles. This role is ideal for a seasoned professional with a strong background in environmental consulting, hazardous materials assessment, regulatory compliance, and client advisory services.

The successful candidate will lead and manage complex environmental investigations, provide technical expertise on hazardous materials and indoor environmental quality issues, and support project delivery for a diverse portfolio of commercial, industrial, institutional, healthcare, and insurance-related clients. In addition to conducting field assessments, this individual will play a key role in client engagement, project oversight, staff mentoring, and technical leadership.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Lead and perform complex environmental investigations, inspections, and monitoring programs related to asbestos, lead-based paint, mold, and other environmental hazards.
* Serve as a technical resource and subject matter expert for hazardous materials assessments, indoor air quality (IAQ) evaluations, and remediation projects.
* Manage field activities, including air, bulk, and surface sampling programs, ensuring compliance with project objectives and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Oversee and interpret environmental data, prepare technical reports, and provide clear recommendations to clients and project stakeholders.
* Direct remediation and abatement oversight activities, including contractor monitoring, final visual inspections, and clearance air sampling.
* Maintain compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, including OSHA, EPA, and CDPH requirements, while ensuring adherence to company health and safety standards.
* Manage project schedules, budgets, and deliverables, ensuring high-quality execution and client satisfaction.
* Develop and maintain strong client relationships by providing technical guidance, regulatory interpretation, and strategic consulting support.
* Mentor and support junior staff through field training, technical review, and professional development initiatives.
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across J.S. Held to support complex projects, business development activities, and practice growth initiatives.
* Contribute to the continuous improvement of technical procedures, quality assurance programs, and best practices within the Industrial Hygiene & Built Environment practice.
* Maintain and calibrate field equipment and ensure proper implementation of quality control and quality assurance procedures.

  
**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Occupational Health, Environmental Engineering, Kinesiology, or a related discipline.
* **5+ years of experience** in industrial hygiene, environmental consulting, hazardous materials management, or a related field, with demonstrated progression in responsibility.
* Extensive experience conducting and managing asbestos, lead-based paint, mold, and indoor air quality investigations.
* Strong knowledge of federal, state, and local regulations, including OSHA, EPA, CDPH, and applicable hazardous materials regulations.
* Experience overseeing environmental sampling programs, including air, bulk, and surface sampling, and interpreting laboratory data.
* Demonstrated experience managing projects, coordinating field teams, and delivering high-quality client deliverables on schedule and within budget.
* Strong technical writing, report preparation, and quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) review experience.
* Ability to independently lead field investigations and travel to project sites throughout the Los Angeles area and surrounding regions.
* Experience serving as a client-facing consultant and providing technical recommendations to stakeholders.
* Valid Driver's License.

**Preferred**

* Certified Site Surveillance Technician (CSST).
* California Lead Sampling Technician Certification.
* NIOSH 582 Microscopy Course (or equivalent).
* OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER Certification.
* Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH), Certified Safety Professional (CSP), or progress toward professional certification.
* EPA AHERA Inspector and/or Management Planner accreditation.
* Experience mentoring junior staff and providing technical oversight.
* Experience supporting business development initiatives, proposal preparation, and client relationship management.
* Experience working on complex commercial, industrial, healthcare, education, or insurance-related projects.

  
**Additional Information**

**Some of the Benefits We Have Include**

J.S. Held understands all our employees are people and sometimes life needs flexibility. We work to always provide an environment that best supports and suits our team’s needs.

* Our flexible work environment allows employees to work remotely, when needed
* Flexible Time Off policy
* Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
* 401k Match
* Commuter Benefit

A reasonable estimate of the salary range for this role is $110,000 - $165,000. Any offered salary range is based on a wide array of fact

Do you want an exciting, dynamic position working with one of California's most charismatic wildlife species? Do you want to use your field biology skills to promote endangered species recovery and resolve human-wildlife conflicts? The Department of Fish and Wildlife's Northern Region is seeking a highly-motivated individual to assist with the state's growing Gray Wolf conservation program.
  
  
This position entails serving as a Gray Wolf biologist for northern California. Key responsibilities include working with the existing Gray Wolf Program biologists to determine the distribution and abundance of Gray Wolves in northern California and their ecological relationships with other wildlife species, prevent Gray Wolf conflicts with livestock production, and contribute to public outreach on Gray Wolf ecology and conservation. The successful candidate will work with a small team of field biologists, driving 4-wheel drive and/or all-terrain vehicles, setting up and monitoring trail cameras, surveying for Gray Wolf tracks, scats and other sign, deploying non-lethal deterrents measures to prevent Gray Wolf conflicts with livestock, and participating in public meetings and other outreach events for parties interested in Gray Wolf ecology and conservation.
  
  
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
  
  
Contribute to field surveys to document the distribution and abundance of Gray Wolves, including camera traps, hand-held telemetry, and survey for tracks, scat and other sign.

Assist with Gray Wolf capture and telemetry collaring efforts.

  
Collect, manage and summarize field data on Gray Wolves, including camera trap videos and biological samples, and contribute to summary reports and management recommendations for CDFW leadership.
  
  
Conduct field investigations of suspected Gray Wolf depredations on livestock.
  
  
Provide technical assistance to livestock producers on the use of non-lethal measures to deter Gray Wolves from livestock areas.
  
  
Participate in public meetings on Gray Wolf ecology and conservation.

Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time. jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**About ADE Consulting Group**
------------------------------

ADE Consulting Group is a leading Australian environmental consultancy providing contaminated land, resource recovery, environmental compliance, occupational hygiene, geotechnical and laboratory services nationwide. We combine expert consulting capability with our own NATA-accredited laboratories and dedicated research and development team to deliver practical, science-based solutions for clients across Australia.

Our environmental team comprises more than 50 consultants nationally, working across major infrastructure, industrial, property, waste, government and energy projects. We pride ourselves on technical excellence, collaboration and developing our people through mentoring, training and exposure to diverse and challenging projects.

**About the Role**
------------------

ADE is seeking an Environmental Scientist to join our team.

This role is suited to an environmental professional with approximately **2 to 6 years of relevant experience** who can independently deliver environmental investigations, contaminated land assessments, groundwater monitoring, waste classification projects and environmental compliance programmes.

You will work closely with experienced Project Managers, Senior Consultants and Principals while continuing to develop your technical expertise, consulting capability and project management skills. The role offers exposure to projects throughout Australia across a broad range of environmental disciplines.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Plan and deliver contaminated land investigations and environmental assessments.
* Undertake soil, groundwater, surface water and waste sampling programmes.
* Develop and refine conceptual site models.
* Interpret laboratory and field data against relevant environmental criteria and guidelines.
* Prepare technical reports, risk assessments and client deliverables.
* Conduct waste classification and resource recovery assessments.
* Support environmental compliance and monitoring programmes.
* Coordinate fieldwork, drilling contractors and other subcontractors.
* Manage project budgets, schedules and project reporting on smaller projects.
* Prepare proposals, fee estimates and variation requests.
* Supervise and mentor graduate consultants and field staff.
* Build and maintain strong client relationships and identify opportunities for repeat work.

**About You**
-------------

To be successful in this role, you will have:

* A Bachelor's degree or higher in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geology, Earth Science, Chemistry or a related discipline.
* Approximately 2-6 years of relevant environmental consulting or environmental industry experience.
* Experience undertaking environmental investigations, field sampling and technical reporting.
* Sound understanding of contaminated land assessment, groundwater monitoring, waste classification, remediation or environmental compliance.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong organisational and project management skills.
* A commitment to workplace health and safety.
* A current Australian Driver Licence.
* Willingness to undertake field work, regional travel and occasional interstate travel.

**Highly Regarded Experience**
------------------------------

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be highly regarded:

* Contaminated land assessment and remediation
* Groundwater assessment and monitoring
* Waste classification and resource recovery
* PFAS investigations
* Asbestos in soil investigations
* Acid sulfate soils
* Environmental due diligence
* Environmental compliance and auditing
* Environmental monitoring programmes

**What We Offer**
-----------------

* Competitive remuneration package with annual salary reviews.
* Flexible working arrangements.
* Genuine career progression opportunities within a national consultancy.
* Ongoing professional development and mentoring from senior technical staff.
* Support for professional memberships and industry involvement.
* Exposure to major projects throughout Australia.
* Collaboration with ADE's multidisciplinary consulting, laboratory and R&D teams.
* A supportive, inclusive and collaborative workplace culture.

**Why Join ADE?**
-----------------

At ADE, you'll work alongside experienced environmental scientists, engineers, geologists and technical specialists on projects that shape how contaminated land, waste and environmental risks are managed across Australia. We invest heavily in developing our people and provide clear career pathways for consultants looking to progress into project management, technical leadership or specialist technical streams.

**How to Apply**
----------------

If you are looking to further your career with a growing national consultancy and enjoy working on technically challenging environmental projects, we encourage you to apply.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**
------------------------------

ADE Consulting Group is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where employment decisions are based on merit, capability, qualifications and business requirements.

Applicants must have the legal right to work in Australia, or be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate Australian work rights.

Please be sure to check your e-mail often for updates. If you do not have an e-mail account on file, Human Resources will send you correspondences via US Mail.***

**TYPICAL DUTIES**
------------------

* Conducts inspections and investigations to determine environmental health problems; determines needs for corrective action and provides appropriate assistance; conducts surveys and collects data.
* Enforces and obtains compliance with federal, state and local laws, ordinances, regulations, and standards in the area of environmental health.
* Inspects food handling and processing establishments, land use applications, public swimming pools and spas, substandard housing, well systems, small public water systems, on-site wastewater treatment and disposal systems, underground storage tank facilities, hazardous waste generator facilities, and other environmental health programs; performs emergency response services.
* Reviews and approves plans for installation of on-site wastewater treatment and disposal systems, well systems, underground storage tanks, public swimming pools, food establishments, small public water systems and other related environmental health installations.
* Investigates complaints of nuisances such as vector problems, waste disposal and other unsanitary conditions; gathers facts, collects samples and prescribes abatement and control measures.
* Inspects chemical and hazardous waste storage facilities and investigates hazardous material spills.
* Gathers, organizes and analyzes technical data and prepares appropriate reports utilizing computers and computer software programs; maintains specialized records; prepares correspondence.
* Interprets environmental health laws and regulations to contractors, public and private officials and the general public; makes presentations to various interest groups.
* Provides information for the preparation of billing statements, issues environmental health permits and collects fees.
* May assist in training of Environmental Health Specialists and Environmental Health Specialist Trainees.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**
--------------------------

**Education:** Possession of a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with course work in sciences and mathematics as prescribed in Section 106600-106735, all inclusive, of the California Health and Safety Code.  
  

**Registration:** Possession of a valid certificate as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist issued by the California Department of Health Services.

  

**License:** Possession of a valid California Driver’s License.

**KNOWLEDGE**
-------------

Basic principles of biology, chemistry, microbiology and physics; principles and practices of environmental health; federal, state and local laws, regulations and standards relative to the duties; agencies, officials and resources involved in the environmental health field; principles and methods of conducting investigations and inspections, methods for resolving problems and enforcement procedures; safety practices; language mechanics; methods of data gathering, analysis and presentation, including statistical concepts; mathematics at the college algebra or calculus level; basic public relations principles.

**ABILITY**
-----------

Conduct inspections, investigations, and reporting procedures; enforce laws and develop satisfactory resolutions of problems and violations; interpret technical written information; communicate effectively with others, both orally and in writing; present information in both written and verbal formats; operate a data entry device; establish and maintain effective working relationships with a wide variety of public and private business officials and the general public; follow written and oral instructions.

**PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS**
--------------------------------

Mobility-Operation of a data entry device; repetitive motion; sitting, standing, walking for extended periods of time; driving; occasional pushing, pulling, bending, squatting, climbing; Lifting-Frequently 5 pounds or less; occasionally 5 to 30 pounds; Visual-Distinguishing between various items, including pests and health conditions; constant good overall vision and reading/close-up work; frequent color perception and use of eye/hand coordination; occasional use of depth perception and peripheral vision; Hearing/Talking-Frequent hearing of normal speech, hearing/talking on the telephone, talking in person; Emotional/Psychological-Frequent decision making, concentration, and public contact; deal with emergency situations, exposure to trauma, grief, death; heights; working with hazardous materials; Special Requirements-Some assignments may require working weekends,

new_jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
new_jobs.description:
**About ADE Consulting Group**
------------------------------

ADE Consulting Group is a leading Australian environmental consultancy providing contaminated land, resource recovery, environmental compliance, occupational hygiene, geotechnical and laboratory services nationwide. We combine expert consulting capability with our own NATA-accredited laboratories and dedicated research and development team to deliver practical, science-based solutions for clients across Australia.

Our environmental team comprises more than 50 consultants nationally, working across major infrastructure, industrial, property, waste, government and energy projects. We pride ourselves on technical excellence, collaboration and developing our people through mentoring, training and exposure to diverse and challenging projects.

**About the Role**
------------------

ADE is seeking an Environmental Scientist to join our team.

This role is suited to an environmental professional with approximately **2 to 6 years of relevant experience** who can independently deliver environmental investigations, contaminated land assessments, groundwater monitoring, waste classification projects and environmental compliance programmes.

You will work closely with experienced Project Managers, Senior Consultants and Principals while continuing to develop your technical expertise, consulting capability and project management skills. The role offers exposure to projects throughout Australia across a broad range of environmental disciplines.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Plan and deliver contaminated land investigations and environmental assessments.
* Undertake soil, groundwater, surface water and waste sampling programmes.
* Develop and refine conceptual site models.
* Interpret laboratory and field data against relevant environmental criteria and guidelines.
* Prepare technical reports, risk assessments and client deliverables.
* Conduct waste classification and resource recovery assessments.
* Support environmental compliance and monitoring programmes.
* Coordinate fieldwork, drilling contractors and other subcontractors.
* Manage project budgets, schedules and project reporting on smaller projects.
* Prepare proposals, fee estimates and variation requests.
* Supervise and mentor graduate consultants and field staff.
* Build and maintain strong client relationships and identify opportunities for repeat work.

**About You**
-------------

To be successful in this role, you will have:

* A Bachelor's degree or higher in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geology, Earth Science, Chemistry or a related discipline.
* Approximately 2-6 years of relevant environmental consulting or environmental industry experience.
* Experience undertaking environmental investigations, field sampling and technical reporting.
* Sound understanding of contaminated land assessment, groundwater monitoring, waste classification, remediation or environmental compliance.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong organisational and project management skills.
* A commitment to workplace health and safety.
* A current Australian Driver Licence.
* Willingness to undertake field work, regional travel and occasional interstate travel.

**Highly Regarded Experience**
------------------------------

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be highly regarded:

* Contaminated land assessment and remediation
* Groundwater assessment and monitoring
* Waste classification and resource recovery
* PFAS investigations
* Asbestos in soil investigations
* Acid sulfate soils
* Environmental due diligence
* Environmental compliance and auditing
* Environmental monitoring programmes

**What We Offer**
-----------------

* Competitive remuneration package with annual salary reviews.
* Flexible working arrangements.
* Genuine career progression opportunities within a national consultancy.
* Ongoing professional development and mentoring from senior technical staff.
* Support for professional memberships and industry involvement.
* Exposure to major projects throughout Australia.
* Collaboration with ADE's multidisciplinary consulting, laboratory and R&D teams.
* A supportive, inclusive and collaborative workplace culture.

**Why Join ADE?**
-----------------

At ADE, you'll work alongside experienced environmental scientists, engineers, geologists and technical specialists on projects that shape how contaminated land, waste and environmental risks are managed across Australia. We invest heavily in developing our people and provide clear career pathways for consultants looking to progress into project management, technical leadership or specialist technical streams.

**How to Apply**
----------------

If you are looking to further your career with a growing national consultancy and enjoy working on technically challenging environmental projects, we encourage you to apply.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**
------------------------------

ADE Consulting Group is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where employment decisions are based on merit, capability, qualifications and business requirements.

Applicants must have the legal right to work in Australia, or be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate Australian work rights.
